question:
Let $*$ be the binary operation on $\mathbb{N}$ defined by $a*b=\operatorname{LCM}(a,b)$.

(i) Find $6*8$ and $9*15$.

(ii) Show that $*$ is commutative.

(iii) Find the identity element and determine which elements of $\mathbb{N}$ are invertible with respect to $*$.
explanation:
(i) Evaluation of the operation
$$6*8=\operatorname{LCM}(6,8)=24$$
and
$$9*15=\operatorname{LCM}(9,15)=45.$$

(ii) Commutativity
For all $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$,
$$\operatorname{LCM}(a,b)=\operatorname{LCM}(b,a).$$
Hence,
$$a*b=b*a,$$
so $*$ is commutative.

(iii) Identity element
For every $a\in\mathbb{N}$,
$$\operatorname{LCM}(a,1)=a.$$
Therefore, $1$ is the identity element.

Invertible elements
If $a$ has an inverse $b$, then
$$a*b=1\Rightarrow\operatorname{LCM}(a,b)=1.$$
This is possible only when $a=b=1$.

Conclusion
The identity element is $1$, and the only invertible element of $\mathbb{N}$ with respect to $*$ is $1$.

options.A: $6*8=14$, $9*15=24$; $*$ is not commutative; the identity is $0$; every element is invertible
options.B: $6*8=48$, $9*15=135$; $*$ is commutative; the identity is $1$; every element is invertible
options.C: $6*8=24$, $9*15=45$; $*$ is commutative; the identity is $1$; only $1$ is invertible
options.D: $6*8=24$, $9*15=45$; $*$ is not commutative; the identity is $0$; no element is invertible
